account:
Today seems to involve ordinary trade surrounded by unconfirmed rumours. During my market walk I heard villagers say the baker carried wheat at the bakery and bread at the inn; I also saw the baker put bread in the market stall chest. At tea, my neighbour said freight had asked the baker about wheat collection and bread deliveries. According to the neighbour, people turned those questions into talk of bridge or port changes, and there was also talk of decorations or a celebration, although the baker knew of no celebration. I have not witnessed any announcement, decorations, or change to transport arrangements. My best explanation is routine supply and delivery business being embellished in conversation, rather than evidence of an organized event or project. Freight's actual plans remain unknown to me.

The builder reported no confirmed damage at the bridge approaches, ferry landing, or warehouse district. He proposed a further inspection for two emeralds, but I authorized neither paid inspection nor repairs, and he acknowledged that decision. At town accounts the secretary had no ledger or verified income and expenses. I checked the treasury myself: 128 emeralds, with none removed. The secretary says my balance report and no-spending decision are recorded in the office chest. The lack of accounting records needs follow-up, but I have no evidence of missing money.

I found my tea host at the east-bank cottage at (16,105), after earlier uncertainty about which neighbour had invited me. The secretary joined us and reminded me of my 16:30 office appointment. It is now 16:07; I have asked whether tomorrow's tea is here too and have not yet heard confirmation. I need to return to the office shortly.
